title: Rate of convergence for the Ramsey ratio R(3,l+1)/R(3,l)

problemStatement.formal: \exists C>0, L_0 \; \forall l>L_0, |R(3,l+1)/R(3,l)-1| \le C\log(l)/l, and \log(l)/l is eventually smaller than 1/\log(l).
problemStatement.plain: The open-question file studies how fast the known k=3 Ramsey ratio approaches 1. It proves an explicit O(log l / l) bound, which is faster than the suggested O(1/log l) benchmark.
whyMatters: Turns a qualitative convergence theorem into a quantitative rate statement.
Separates the solved k=3 case from the conditional general-k asymptotic discussion.

proven: `rate_of_convergence_k3` proves the k=3 ratio error is bounded by C*log(l)/l for large l.
`log_over_l_faster_than_inv_log` proves log(l)/l is eventually smaller than 1/log(l).
`rate_is_O_log_over_l_not_inv_log` packages the rate bound with the comparison.
`conditional_convergence_general_k` delegates the general-k convergence statement to the parent asymptotic-ratio theorem.
open: The general-k rate needs quantitative asymptotics for R(k,l), not just convergence to the conjectured main term.
The imported Ramsey-number infrastructure carries the deeper combinatorial assumptions from the parent file.
knownResults.goal: Use the OQ-02 file as the quantitative-rate entry: preserve the proved k=3 O(log l / l) bound and make future general-k work state the required asymptotic hypotheses explicitly.

currentState.focus: Initial problem understanding. Read problem.md and gather context.

knowledge.progressSummary: PROGRESS: Verified 2 actual sorries in conditional_rate_general_k. Main results sorry-free. Sorries need Bernoulli bounds and ratio decomposition. Hypothesis quantifier order may need reformulation.
insights: Rate of convergence for k=3 is O(log l / l), from recurrence + Kim lower bound
This is FASTER than O(1/log l) because (log l)^2 < l for large l
Explicit constant: C = 2/c where c is Kim lower bound constant
For general k with power-law asymptotics, rate would be O(1/l)
The Ramsey recurrence R(3,l+1) <= R(3,l) + (l+1) is the key structural input
2 actual sorries in conditional_rate_general_k (lines 179, 209). Main results (rate_of_convergence_k3, log_over_l_faster_than_inv_log) are sorry-free.
Sorry #1 (line 179): Bernoulli-type bound |((l+1)/l)^(k-1)·(log l/log(l+1))^(k-2) - 1| ≤ 2k/l needs real analysis (exp bounds, log comparison)
Sorry #2 (line 209): Ratio decomposition R"/R = (R"/g")·(g"/g)·(g/R) needs careful bound propagation
Hypothesis quantifier structure is ∀ε ∃c (c depends on ε), weaker than standard asymptotic ∃c ∀ε. This may make the O(1/l) rate unprovable as stated.
nextSteps: Eliminate 2 sorries in conditional_rate_general_k (growth ratio bound)
Consider if the O(log l/l) rate is tight or could be improved to O(1/l)
